title: UK Bakes in Hottest May Day Ever — Donkeys Get the Day Off!
summary: Imagine stepping outside and feeling like you're in an oven. That's what happened in the UK on Monday when temperatures soared to 34.8°C (about 95°F) in London. That's the hottest May day the country has ever seen! Wales also broke its record with 32.2°C. The heat was so intense that a donkey derby in Surrey had to cancel the donkey races and dog show to keep the animals safe. Even at night, it barely cooled down — London had its warmest May night ever at 19.4°C. Normally, late May is around 14-20°C. The UK Health Security Agency issued an amber heat-health alert, which means people should be extra careful. Some towns even lost water because everyone was using so much. The AA warned drivers not to leave kids or pets in parked cars, where it can get as hot as 60°C inside! Despite the heat, thousands watched the famous cheese-rolling race in Gloucestershire, where people chase a giant wheel of cheese down a steep hill. A German YouTuber won this year. Forecasters say it could hit 35°C on Tuesday, with possible thunderstorms later.
why_it_matters: It reminds us that hot weather can be dangerous, so we should drink water and not stay in hot cars, and it's important to look after our pets and ourselves during a heatwave.

background_read: The UK (United Kingdom) is a group of countries in Europe that includes England, Scotland, Wales, and Northern Ireland.
Summer heatwaves are rare there, so very hot days often break records.
The Automobile Association (AA) is a big group that helps drivers with breakdowns and safety advice.
Article_Structure: WHO: People in the UK, including children, drivers, and animals, as well as forecasters and the AA.
WHAT: The UK experienced its hottest May day ever, reaching 34.8°C in London, with a heat-health alert, cancelled events, and water shortages.
WHERE: Across the UK, especially London, Wales, Surrey, and Gloucestershire.
WHY: A heatwave brought extreme temperatures, far above normal for late May.

perspectives.description: Many people enjoyed the unusual weather, with thousands gathering to watch the cheese-rolling race and making the most of the sunny day.
The heat was dangerous, leading to health alerts, a cancelled donkey derby, and water shortages in some towns.
Forecasters warned about the record temperatures and predicted thunderstorms, keeping an eye on the situation.
